content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated pre‑lightened coffee is made from selected Arabica beans from which almost all caffeine has been removed. Pre‑lightening refers to a mild roast level that preserves a gentle aroma and a subtle acidity. This coffee is ideal for those who want the flavor without the stimulating effect.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is commonly performed using water, CO₂ or solvent methods, after which the beans are roasted.
Pre‑lightened beans retain more chlorophyll, giving them a lighter color and a mild bitterness.
Decaf coffee may contain up to 0.1 % caffeine, which is practically negligible.
The flavor of pre‑lightened coffee is often described as “floral” and “fruity,” unlike dark roasts.
Decaf coffee is frequently used in desserts where coffee flavor is desired without a stimulant effect.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Even without caffeine, pre‑lightened coffee retains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Coffee stimulates gastric juice production, which can aid digestion without causing nervous stimulation.

items.title: May lower diabetes risk
items.content: Regular consumption of decaf coffee has been linked to a reduced risk of type 2 diabetes.

items.title: Liver protection
items.content: Polysaccharides and chlorogenic acids in coffee may contribute to liver health.

items.title: Mild acidity
items.content: Pre‑lightened roast has a softer acidity, making it gentler on the stomach.

items.title: Coffee allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to coffee components, including aromatic compounds.

items.title: Residual solvents
items.content: When solvent decaffeination is used, choose products that have passed strict quality controls to avoid chemical residues.

items.title: Acidity for sensitive stomachs
items.content: Although milder, pre‑lightened coffee can still cause discomfort in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Even trace caffeine may affect certain medications, especially central nervous system stimulants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use 1‑2 tsp of ground coffee per 180‑200 ml of hot water (90‑95 °C) and steep for 3‑4 minutes. Suitable as a hot beverage or cold brew. Add milk, plant‑based cream, or a light sweetener if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store coffee in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep it in the refrigerator, but protect it from moisture condensation.
